composition.story: How does RLHF turn human feedback into model behavior? Start with two answers from an instruction-tuned Answer model. Follow Human ranking into Reward model training. Advance to Reward-guided update to see how learned reward changes the Answer model. Use Previous and Next to inspect each state.

aha.observation: Human rankings train a reward model; reinforcement learning uses its scores to make higher-reward answers more likely.

parts.presentation: Place below the explanation and instructions. Show the active state and completed trace here, not inside the picture.
Use the canonical pipeline arrangement with fixed named regions and wrapped labels. Change one region's highlight at a time. Keep every region stationary.
Anchor to the highlighted region. Explain its role without duplicating readout values.
Place below the picture. Reserve the last row for bound status. These categorical readouts use no units, numerical scales, or rounding.

controls.label: Training state
controls.presentation: Provide Previous and Next with accessible names, visible focus, and keyboard operation. Preserve names when disabled at boundaries. Default to the first state. Bounds are the first and last states; each action advances one state. Every state persists until another action. Capture Reward-guided update as the reference state.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore the first state and all defaults. Support keyboard activation and visible focus. Brief parameter-control budget: zero. Navigation and Reset are separate from that budget.

regions.label: Answer model
values: Prompt: Explain rain to a child.
Answer A: Water falls from clouds.

states.label: Generate answers
states.sentence: The instruction-tuned Answer model generates two candidate answers to the same prompt.
states.why: The prompt and candidate answers stay fixed throughout this simplified example.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Candidates available; human feedback not collected.

states.label: Collect human ranking
states.sentence: The human reviewer compares the candidates for clarity to a child.
states.why: This fixed, illustrative preference supplies training feedback; the Answer model has not changed.

readouts.label: Human preference
readouts.value: Answer A preferred over Answer B.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Human ranking collected; Answer model unchanged.

states.label: Train reward model
states.sentence: The Reward model learns to predict human rankings, providing a scoring signal for reinforcement learning.
states.why: Real training uses many comparisons; this illustration assumes the Reward model reproduces the example preference.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Reward model trained; Answer model unchanged.

states.label: Reward-guided update
states.sentence: Reinforcement learning updates the Answer model using Reward model scores rather than another human vote.
states.why: The illustrated update increases the likelihood of the higher-reward answer; learned reward remains an imperfect proxy for human preferences.

readouts.label: Update signal
readouts.value: Reward model scores, learned from Human ranking.

readouts.label: Compared with before the update
readouts.value: Answer A is now more likely.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Reward-guided update complete; held for inspection.

2.reason: The reward-guided-update state is the reference state, and its status readout says "held for inspection", so it persists until the learner acts.

7.reason: The picture is a fixed three-region layout where only one highlight changes at a time, and the readouts stay to one to three short rows, which suits brief depth.
